When you say "both actions would be complete before the harp is destroyed", I read that as "both actions would be [resolved] before the harp is destroyed", which is in fact incorrect, as you also point out that "you have to resolve them in order" which is correct.

In a nutshell, the Harp is a Power, and power effects are sourced to the Hero using them. Activating the Power triggers the powers instructions. The Harp has [1] intruction with multiple effects. Both effects simultaniously and imediatly get added to our theoretical "stack of effects to be resolved" becuase they are contained within one intruction. Once there are no more triggered instructions to add, now you start to resolve in the order in which they appear in the stack (which correlates to the order in which they appeared on the initial instruction). Because of the Official Ruling where effects do not resolve simultaniously, the Perform text resolves first, destroying the Harp. Then the Accompany effect resolves as it was next in the stack and its source (Argent Adept) is presumably still active. Had any other intructions triggered in the middle of any of that, they would get added to the top of the stack instantly and resolving the stack continues with the newest effect added.

Again, I think we are saying the same thing here. There is no consistancy in the terms we are using however, as we both are defining certain words differently. Thats sorta why I am trying to refine my approach to resolving effects, and hopefully we can start talking in the same language here.

The Accompany text is NOT dependant upon the Perform text happening, only that the Power was activated in the first place. 

Straight from the EE rulebook, top of page 8: "…there are situations in which multiple effects would occur simultaneously" (like 2 effects having the same trigger like the Harp). "In all situations, card effects that happen simultaneously occur in the order in which the cards entered play". That last sentence has been extended in rulings to include the order in which effects appear on a single card, not just accross different cards.

The Harp is not the source of the Perform and Accompany effects. It is Argent. I do not see how you could argue that point otherwise.
